speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the number of illegal vape sellers and buyers apprehended in the last three years; (b) how many of these purchases were made online and through physical stores; (c) what have been the actions taken against these offenders; and (d) what more can the Ministry do to deter the purchase and sale of illegal vapes in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The enforcement actions taken against these offenders depended on the merits of each case and included prosecution, composition fines or a warning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: HSA will continue to work with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority and the Singapore Police Force to deter the illegal import, sale and purchase of vaporisers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Besides enforcement, the Health Promotion Board will continue to educate Singaporeans regarding the harmful effects of vaporisers and correct any misconception that vaporisers conclusively help with smoking cessation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: At the same time, we will strengthen smoking cessation programmes so that smokers can access proven therapies and methods to help them quit smoking.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My first supplementary question relates to these illegal vapes also being sold in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Besides online sales, according to news reports last month, illegal vaporisers are also being sold in our neighbourhoods, including busy shopping districts such as Orchard Road.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Buyers and sellers, according to the news report, used code words, such as "cartridges" or "juices", to facilitate all these under-the-table illegal sales.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can I ask that we also step up our enforcement in these areas, especially in the neighbourhoods?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My second question relates to a recent study done in the United Kingdom (UK) on adults attending the UK National Health Service's Stop Smoking Programme.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On the first point, to step up enforcement, we will do so.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have been working closely with online platforms, such as Carousell and Instagram, to stamp out online sale of vaporisers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: With regard to physical sales, we have conducted intelligence, surprise raids, but we will take into consideration the Member's suggestions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: If the Member has specific leads, please do share with us.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On the second question, I believe the Member is referring to the study done in UK on adults attending National Health Service's Stop Smoking Services.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: That study involved 900 smokers with good motivation to quit.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is compared with 10% of smokers from the NRT group.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: However, in the e-cigarette group, 80% of those who quit smoking continued to use e-cigarettes 12 months later.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This means that, overall, less than 4% of those in the e-cigarette group quit tobacco product use and their nicotine addiction totally.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As there are concerns about the potential harmful effects of the long-term use of e-cigarettes – the Member may know about the debate in the United States where e-cigarettes have been linked to lung injury – this raises the question whether they would have been better off quitting using other more proven established methods.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In addition, more than 30% of those in the e-cigarette group who failed to quit ended up using both e-cigarettes and cigarettes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This actually leaves them worse off than before, as a recent large study had shown that dual users of cigarettes and e-cigarettes are actually exposed to more toxins than persons who only smoke cigarettes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Ministry's position is that there is currently limited evidence on the safety and efficacy of e-cigarettes as a smoking cessation product.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But we will continue to monitor emerging evidence and studies like the ones mentioned by Mr Melvin Yong.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Our regulation and public health policies are evidence-based and if there is robust evidence that any particular product can safely help smokers completely stop using tobacco or nicotine, we will be happy to consider these options.
